findings.summary: The right panel of docs/figures/kernel-compile-barrier/compile-pass-profile/time-per-pass.svg is labelled 'seconds of the compile wall' and presents its three bars as a split of that wall, but they sum to 99.235 s against the 96.116 s compile wall the same receipt reports (attributed 92.098 + before-first-dump 3.4452 + after-last-dump 3.6917), so a reader who adds the bars exceeds the wall the axis names. The three bars partition the pass-dump chain, not the compile wall, and the 95.8% coverage the fragment headlines divides 92.098 by the different 96.116 figure, so neither the wall total nor the coverage percentage can be read off the figure. A wall reference line at compile_seconds, or a y-label naming the chain wall with a stated denominator, would let a reader check the panel's own claim.

The left panel labels every row with the last path component of its dump key, so two rows read as file names rather than passes - 'jit__lambda.ir-no-opt.ll' (4.2 s) and 'jit__lambda.priority_fusion_dump.txt' (1.2 s) - while the evidence table names the same rows ir-no-opt and priority_fusion_dump. The rendered bars also give a reader no way to tell a single-pass row from an aggregate: ir-no-opt.ll is 253 dumps and ir-with-opt.ll is 253, zero_sized_hlo_elimination is 18 and dce is 11, all drawn identically to the one-dump rows beside them, so 4.2 s reads as one expensive pass when it is the summed LLVM IR stage.

The positive-control figures are drawn as a four-line block of prose inside the right axes ('control 1024-op chain: 7.72 s, 95% attributed' and 'control 64-op chain: 0.74 s, 11% attributed'). Two rows of two numbers is naturally a table, and in the picture the block reads as an annotation of the point-jet bars rather than as the control measurement the run's done-when (2) requires, so a reader skimming the figure can miss that the same instrument attributed 95% of a 7.72 s compile and only 11% of a 0.74 s one.

The blue/grey split of the left panel's bars carries meaning that appears nowhere in the picture: grey marks the codegen stages and blue the HLO passes, and only the figcaption in the evidence fragment says so. There is no legend and no direct label, so a reader who sees the figure without its caption has two colours and no key.

rubric_verdicts.contrast: pass - value and tick text is #333333 on white at about 12.6:1, and both bar fills clear 3:1 (blue #3b6ea5 about 5.2:1, grey #929292 about 3.1:1)
rubric_verdicts.data_ink: pass - two plain bar panels on white; the ink is bars, value labels and the two axis labels, with no fill or gradient carrying information
rubric_verdicts.decoration: pass - no gridlines, no background fill, no shading, no styling theme; top and right spines removed on both panels
rubric_verdicts.label_collision: pass - no text is clipped or overlapping: rendered ink spans columns 13-1382 of 1400 and rows 20-698 of 720, the right panel's control block ends 88 px short of the right edge, and no label touches a bar or another label
rubric_verdicts.legibility: pass - both panels read at a glance: 14 pt ticks and 16 pt axis labels on a 1400x720 canvas, every bar carrying its own value label, and the longest tick label (jit__lambda.priority_fusion_dump.txt) clearing the canvas edge by 13 px
rubric_verdicts.table_form: defect - the right panel's four-line control block states two rows of two numbers (wall and attributed share for the 1024-op and 64-op controls) as running prose, which is a small table drawn as text; the bar panels themselves plot a part-to-whole relationship and are not a table in image form
